sections.heading: 1. How to start
lines: ① Start with 15–20 min, 2–3 times a week.
② Take rest breaks at the wall.
③ Same or better next day? Add a few minutes.
④ Breaststroke sore? Try backstroke instead.

sections.heading: 2. Stop and get checked if…
lines: Your back is clearly worse the next day —
drop the volume and get advice.

slides.heading: See your GP promptly if

caption:
Koko wondered if swimming was a good idea with a sore back. Often, yes. Water takes some of your weight and removes impact, so many people find the pool a comfortable way to stay active.

In freestyle, roll your body to breathe rather than lifting your head high. If breaststroke grumbles, swap in backstroke or deep-water jogging. Start with 15 to 20 minutes a few times a week and build up if your back feels the same or better next day. It suits alongside walking and strength work.

Pain that wakes you, numbness around the groin, bladder or bowel changes, leg weakness or fever need a prompt GP check. Our Sydney CBD and Chatswood physios can help you plan your laps. Book online via the link in bio.

General information only — not a substitute for an individual assessment.
